name: hardroad.default
description: Evidence-based default agent workflow: cheap parallel read-only exploration -> frontier planning -> delegation-aware implementation (single writer) -> clean-context diff review -> deterministic verification -> bounded fix/replan loop -> report with telemetry.

meta.source: Cognition 'Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working'; Cognition Devin Fusion; Cognition 'Making Fable Cheaper Than Opus'; Anthropic multi-agent research system; LangChain read-vs-write parallelization; Co-Coder communication/compute tradeoff; OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.

review.role: clean-context diff review; cross-vendor blind-spot coverage

explorer.prompt: Read the target repo scope, map relevant code and docs, and return file paths + snippets. Do not modify anything.

planner.prompt: Write a spec-quality brief: goal, constraints, edge cases, definition of done, and a decision on delegability. Never dictate full file contents - state outcomes and constraints.

writer.prompt: Implement per the spec. Single writer: make all edits yourself, in a coherent thread.

sidekick.prompt: Apply the spec exactly. The plan is fixed: do not design, just implement and run the verification the main agent specified.

reviewer.prompt: You are a clean-context reviewer. You did not write this code. Review the diff only, then re-discover context. Flag bugs, blind spots, spec non-compliance with severity and file:line.

explore_repo.description: One read-only cheap exploration pass over a repo scope. Perfectly parallelizable: reads only, no writes, isolated context.

fix_attempt.description: A bounded corrective pass: writer responds to review + verification feedback, then re-verifies.

explore.label: Explore sub-repos (cheap, read-only, parallel)
explore.description: Fan out one cheap read-only agent per scope. Research: reads parallelize cleanly; context isolation keeps the frontier context lean.

plan.label: Plan (frontier, single writer)
plan.description: Frontier model owns the judgment. Produces a spec artifact - outcome constraints, not dictated code.

evidence.finding: Frontier intelligence should be spent on the plan, ambiguity, and final review - not on mechanical volume.
The quality lever is the brief: enumerate constraints, edge cases, and a definition of done. Fable's constraint-rich briefs beat Opus's dictated file contents.
An implementation plan is a first-class artifact you can read, diff, and gate before any side effect fires.

route.label: Route by delegability
route.description: Judgment decides: mechanical+safe -> cheap sidekick; judgement-bound or serial-debug -> frontier writer stays on it. Research: 'the same judgment that writes a good brief also knows when not to write one.'

evidence.finding: Delegation controls what work stays with the expensive model; routing decides whether the expensive model is involved at all.
Forcing delegation decreases performance - it just delegates the wrong things. Delegability is itself a judgment call.
When the judgment IS the deliverable, delegating it backfires (hard React feature scored 27/100). Mechanical work hands off cleanly.

implement_sidekick.label: Implement (cheap sidekick)
implement_sidekick.description: Fixed spec, mechanical work: cheap model does the volume. Writes stay single-threaded - exactly one writer, never parallel writers.

evidence.finding: Once the plan is fixed, throughput and cost matter more than raw IQ.
Writes must stay single-threaded; parallel writes fragment implicit decisions.

implement_frontier.label: Implement (frontier writer)
implement_frontier.description: Judgement-bound task: frontier model stays the single writer for the whole thread.

review.label: Review diff (clean context, other family)
review.description: Read-only agent with a fresh context that sees the diff, never the author's session. Different model family when possible. Highest-leverage addition.

evidence.finding: A clean-context reviewer with no shared context catches bugs the author cannot see; shorter context = more intelligence on the diff.
Main and sidekick from different vendors means every diff gets an independent second-family read.
The model that wrote the code is often the worst reviewer of it.

verify.label: Verify (deterministic gates)
verify.description: Lint + tests + typecheck as the gate. Never trust model self-evaluation.

evidence.finding: Automated quality gates are structural: each agent's output passes tests before merge eligibility.
Verification is a structural orchestration component separate from execution agents.

quality_gate.label: Quality gate (bounded retry)
quality_gate.description: Pass -> report. Fail -> bounded fix loop via subflow. Guard counts loopbacks; exhaust -> replan.

evidence.finding: Loop generation + evaluation must be bounded; unbounded loops drift. Guard counts loopbacks, exhaust routes to replan.

fix.label: Fix loop (bounded)
fix.description: Bounded corrective iteration; each pass records loops + cost to the ledger.

evidence.finding: Evaluator-optimizer: loop generation + evaluation; must be bounded to stay accurate.
Bounded multi-attempt retry lifts pass rate (81.2% pass@3 vs single-attempt baselines).

replan.label: Replan (frontier escape hatch)
replan.description: Fix cycle exhausted or gate mis-routed: frontier re-owns the design, then re-enters the routing choice.

report.label: Report + telemetry
report.description: Final summary, per-state cost ledger (OTel-aligned), and a rating hook for the efficiency UI.
